title: Make invocation token totals agree with per-model usage and the gate
summary: The gate's reconciliation rule compares the requested model's modelUsage tokens with the invocation's tokens, which come from the result event's top-level usage. In job 2fsa those disagreed (90/52656/3634696/134508 vs 6/3136/275219/3821). I read the request as: fix the root cause so records Athena writes always reconcile, and have the gate check the same quantity. The audience is the Athena owner, who needs verified jobs to land.

defaults_applied.how: Fix how the invocation's tokens are derived and make the gate check the same quantity, instead of relaxing the gate for one job.
Add regression tests, with cargo test and clippy clean.
Criteria run a reconciliation over an event shaped like the failing one.
One focused change across the agent stream parsing and the gate.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Root cause: the result event's top-level usage covers less than modelUsage, probably the main thread only. modelUsage also includes subagent or other-turn usage. I inferred this from reading stream.rs and reconcile.rs. I did not see the failing record.

The preferred fix is to make the recorded invocation tokens come from modelUsage when it is present, and to keep top-level usage as the fallback. The gate then compares the sum over all models. Loosening the gate alone would leave the records disagreeing internally.
No governance file changes are needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a new test feeds a result event whose top-level usage differs from modelUsage (a main thread plus subagent usage on the requested model). It shows the resulting invocation record passes check_invocation with no Reconciliation violation.
Run cargo test: a reconcile test shows that an invocation whose measured tokens genuinely disagree with its per-model usage is still flagged.

The invocation's measured tokens and the gate's check use one definition. The definition is stated in a doc comment: either the sum of modelUsage over all models or the requested model's modelUsage. The gate compares like with like.
Run cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check: both are clean. Existing stream and claude tests still pass.
The defect's numbers (90/52656/3634696/134508 against 6/3136/275219/3821) appear in a regression test fixture or comment, so the owner can see the job 2fsa failure is covered.

out_of_scope: Re-landing job 20261015-131540-2fsa or editing its records
Changing the study or explainer content of that job
Altering cost reconciliation or outcome-total reconciliation beyond what the token fix requires
departures: Slightly higher cost than the reference: the fix spans two crates, and the root cause is an inference I did not confirm against the failing record.
